:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_s3_object.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

`module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` already depends on `aws_s3_object.this` implicitly — its `spark_history_server_helm_config` interpolates `aws_s3_object.this.key` (visible in the graph's implicit_deps). The explicit `depends_on` entry for `aws_s3_object.this` therefore duplicates an existing dependency.

`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` sets `node_role_arn = ... aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn` (present in the graph's implicit_deps), so the explicit `depends_on` entry for `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` duplicates a dependency already established by that attribute reference.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` interpolates `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id` in its local-exec command (an implicit dependency already captured in the graph), so the explicit `depends_on` entry for `aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution` is redundant.

`null_resource.update_trust_policy` interpolates `kubernetes_namespace.spark.id` in its local-exec command (an implicit dependency already captured in the graph), so the explicit `depends_on` entry for `kubernetes_namespace.spark` is redundant.

`module.aws_eks_teams` creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC and service accounts against the cluster's API server, but it only depends on `module.aws_eks` (cluster creation) and never waits for the cluster-readiness gate. Unlike the managed/self-managed node-group and EMR modules (which all `depends_on = [kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth]`), this module can try to talk to the API server before the control plane is reachable/aws-auth is configured. It should depend on `kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth` (which itself depends on `data.http.eks_cluster_readiness`).
